method: Publisher pages opened and read on 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-24; concise paraphrases for this authorized acceptance batch, not independent experiments

checks.facts: README lists NVIDIA SM100 and Huawei Ascend 950. KV cache system, prefill/decode disaggregation and replica load balancing are required service components not included in this release. License is Apache-2.0. NVIDIA-only invariance and deterministic sampling are explicitly qualified.
checks.must_keep: Engine release is distinct from a complete serving system; do not equate off-list hardware with an independently tested impossibility.

checks.facts: The team reports 155 trillion tokens/day per cluster and US$38 revenue per GPU-hour at valley pricing. Revenue is not profit. Deployment conditions and concurrency matter to optimizations.
checks.must_keep: Attribute figures to the team and retain pricing basis; no investment-return promise or universal acceleration claim.

checks.facts: Executable worlds combine files/CLI, MCP services and mirrored websites. Two-stage synthesis includes task verifiers and quality gates. 341 environment-task pairs and model links are available. Evaluation table explicitly lists eight external benchmarks with task counts and metric types.
checks.must_keep: Release and model self-report are distinct from independent reproduction. Do not say the benchmark names are undisclosed.

checks.facts: README describes coding-agent animation, composition and point-at-frame edits and links demonstrations. Code/documents use MIT; bundled third-party parts and the author's character have separately stated conditions.
checks.must_keep: Project claims and demonstrations do not prove our own tested quality. Summary omitted license/effect information is not proof the repository omits it. Historical popularity is a dated snapshot.

checks.facts: TorchNeuron is a native PyTorch backend for Trainium, announced for public beta October 20 under Apache-2.0. It supports eager execution, torch.compile and NKI on Trainium2/3.
checks.must_keep: Supported platforms and beta scope; backend compatibility is not a universal measured performance improvement.

checks.facts: Article names Perryman for titanium and Qnity Electronics for camera films, specific iPhone products, a commitment of up to US$100 million over three years with Perryman, within Apple's four-year US$600 billion manufacturing commitment.
checks.must_keep: Commitment is not money already spent, and is distinct from the Perryman amount. The original article has concrete materials, products and periods; do not claim it gives none.

checks.facts: Reports SIA concerns about vulnerable and opaque inputs and calls for government-industry coordination over onshoring and stockpiling.
checks.must_keep: Association assessment and requested action are distinct from a policy already implemented; vulnerability does not prove no substitute can exist.

checks.facts: Reports economist Adam Hersh's analysis that no operating US smelter can produce military-specific high-purity aluminum, with exposure to potential supply disruptions. This does not mean the US has no ordinary aluminum production.
checks.must_keep: Military-specific scope, report attribution; not a claim that the US has no aluminum smelters of any kind.

checks.facts: Research concerns chip-scale frequency combs as rulers for light and components for portable optical clocks. NIST/JQI describe a two-laser microresonator approach and potential navigation applications.
checks.must_keep: Potential research application is not an already deployed backup-navigation product.

checks.facts: Article describes Google's demand-response VPP agreement with Voltus. Its earlier 100 MW agreement is one-tenth the new deal; Google's data-center growth and grid constraints are the context. The deal appears largest of its kind from a hyperscaler.
checks.must_keep: Demand-side grid flexibility is distinct from building a new generating plant. 'Appears largest of its kind' must not become an unqualified world's-largest claim. Do not say capacity is not given.

checks.facts: Article identifies the university and describes seismic imaging, rock microscopy and simulations. Reported estimates: 160 m impactor, roughly 43–46 million years ago, crater buried 700 m below seabed, waves over 100 m. Underlying Nature Communications paper is dated 2025.
checks.must_keep: Estimated ancient event and research reconstruction, not a modern warning forecast. News article date differs from underlying study date; do not claim methods or institution are absent.

checks.facts: Reports improvements after a 12-week short daily resistance-exercise intervention in adults 65 or older, including strength, balance and rising from a chair.
checks.must_keep: Study population and duration; no guarantee for every person and no clinical treatment recommendation.

checks.facts: Study followed 13 ISS astronauts for about six months. Intensive daily exercise and simulated Martian gravity after return are part of the reported context.
checks.must_keep: Simulated conditions in studied astronauts do not demonstrate all risks of an actual Mars mission are resolved.

checks.facts: Laboratory research links excess RNA during poxvirus infection with mitochondrial impairment and possible disease implications.
checks.must_keep: Experimental context and potential implications; not proof of a clinical disease cause or a vaccine safety conclusion.

checks.facts: Article distinguishes the Hsi/Ho legend from documented history and presents named scholars' differing interpretations; versions differ in date and even whether an eclipse was involved.
checks.must_keep: Legend, expert interpretation and documented history remain distinct; do not assert the named execution as established fact or claim no interpretive basis is described.

checks.facts: Article describes the planned 2027–2031 runestone project and Denmark's approximately 260 surviving runestones. It names funding and institutions.
checks.must_keep: Planned research and proposed questions are not already established political-network findings. Do not claim no dates or scale appear in the article.

checks.facts: Article describes radiocarbon dating of two Italian oak populations and an interpretation linking reduced human pressure after the Black Death with forest regeneration.
checks.must_keep: Specific populations and historical inference, not all-European forests or a method-free claim.

checks.facts: Library describes Mary Lincoln's February 15, 1865 letter to Caroline Wright and provides a link to the digitized letter, roughly two months before Abraham Lincoln's assassination.
checks.must_keep: Emotion is a historian's reading of this letter, not a complete psychological judgment of the writer.

checks.facts: Paper describes executable PC worlds with shared GUI/MCP/CLI state, task/verifier co-synthesis, heterogeneous execution checks and counterfactual probes. Authors release 341 environment-task pairs, report GPT-6-Astra solving 60%, and report two Qwen models improving across eight named OOD benchmarks. Sections 5.2 and 5.3 present quality-gate and RL ablations; appendices list evaluation protocols and benchmarks.
checks.must_keep: Author-reported results under the described protocol; do not claim there are no ablations, benchmark names or per-benchmark results. Hypotheses about harness effects remain hypotheses, not established contamination or the sole explanation.

checks.facts: Article relays a reported Microsoft internal projection of US$1,200–1,800 for Project Helix. Hardware subsidies could lower the price. Neither company has publicly commented on expected next-generation retail prices; official release dates have not been announced. The article does discuss reported launch targets.
checks.must_keep: Reported projection, not confirmed retail pricing. Do not say the article contains no launch timing. Component-cost explanation is attributed to the article.

checks.facts: University reports newly available seismic data, microscopic analysis of oil-well rock cuttings, shocked quartz/feldspar at crater-floor depth and numerical models. The team estimates a 160 m impactor about 43–46 million years ago; crater is buried 700 m below the seabed, and reconstructed waves exceed 100 m. This is a 2025 research announcement.
checks.must_keep: Do not invent the exact chronological research procedure or assert that every evidence type was directly input to the numerical model. Methods provide complementary evidence; reconstructed ancient event is distinct from present-day warning.
